title: Checkpoint: Evolution
objective: After this level you can explain how natural selection and fossils show that life changes over time.
summary: In science a theory is an explanation backed by vast evidence. This chapter caught evolution being watched (finches, moths) and dug up (Archaeopteryx, Tiktaalik, Pakicetus).

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: 'Evolution is just a theory.' Yes, in the science sense.
cards.body: In everyday talk, a theory is a hunch. In science, it's the top of the ladder. This chapter gave you the evidence. Here's what the word really means, and how the pieces fit.

cards.headline: A hunch or a heavyweight?
cards.body: When you say 'I have a theory', you usually mean a guess. In science, a theory is a comprehensive explanation of some part of nature, backed by a vast body of evidence, like the theory that living things are made of cells. Evolution is a theory in that sense. The National Academy of Sciences says there is no scientific controversy about its basic facts: it has survived testing by many thousands of scientists for more than a century.

cards.headline: Two ways this chapter caught evolution

items.label: Watched it happen
points: Grants' finches: bigger beaks after the 1977 drought
Peppered moths: dark, then rarer again

items.label: Dug it up
points: Tiktaalik: a fish with wrist bones, found where predicted
Pakicetus: a whale's ear on a land mammal

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How natural selection works, and how drought-hit finches and soot-darkened moths let people watch it.
What Darwin's fossil sloths and island-by-island mockingbirds hinted about how species change.
How fossils and rock layers trace life's history, from fish onto land to whales back into the sea.
Why birds are the dinosaurs that survived when an asteroid wiped out all the rest.

questions.prompt: Evolution recap: what does 'theory' mean in science?

options.label: A guess that hasn't been tested yet
An explanation backed by vast evidence
A rule that can never change

questions.explanation: A scientific theory is a comprehensive explanation of some aspect of nature supported by a vast body of evidence.

questions.prompt: Evolution recap: how did Tiktaalik add to confidence in evolutionary theory?

options.label: It was found where the theory predicted
It was the first fossil ever dated
It was a living fish in the Arctic
It proved fish can breathe air
options.rationale: The point was the successful prediction.

questions.explanation: Its finders predicted the age and type of rock to search, and found it there; a confirmed prediction strengthens a theory.

questions.prompt: Evolution recap, from Level 82: after the 1977 drought, which medium ground finches survived best on Daphne Major?

options.label: Those with longer wings
options.rationale: Beaks, not wings, made the difference.

options.label: Those with brighter feathers
options.rationale: Beaks, not colors, made the difference.

questions.explanation: Only big, hard seeds were left, and larger beaks could crack them.

questions.prompt: Evolution recap, from Level 86: where is the crater linked to the end-Cretaceous extinction?
questions.explanation: The Chicxulub crater is centred on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula.

questions.prompt: Evolution recap: what do Archaeopteryx and Pakicetus have in common?

options.label: Both lived in the sea
options.rationale: Pakicetus lived by the water's edge, Archaeopteryx on land.

options.label: Both mix features of old and new groups
Both died in the Chicxulub impact

questions.explanation: Archaeopteryx mixes bird and dinosaur features; Pakicetus pairs a land body with a whale's ear.
